data.label: Trigger Account Monitor
data.description: Begin monitoring existing customer accounts for churn-risk signals.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic workflow trigger with no decisioning, prediction, or language understanding. L0 is sufficient because it simply initiates the automation on a schedule or event.

data.label: Collect Usage Data
data.description: Retrieve recent product usage and calculate the 30-day usage trend for each account.
data.rationale: Retrieving usage records and calculating a 30-day trend can be handled with deterministic data access and arithmetic. L0 applies because this is rule-based computation without uncertainty or machine learning.

data.label: Collect Support Signals
data.description: Fetch support tickets and identify tickets tagged with negative sentiment.
data.rationale: Fetching tickets is deterministic, but identifying negative sentiment from ticket text requires language understanding. L2 is appropriate because this step performs NLP/NLU-style sentiment classification rather than generation.

data.label: Collect Billing Signals
data.description: Check invoice history for late or failed payments for each account.
data.rationale: This is a straightforward lookup and rule-based flagging task. L0 is enough because late or failed payments can be detected from structured billing records without ML or language processing.

data.label: Score Churn Risk
data.description: Combine usage, support, and billing signals into a churn-risk score from 0 to 100.
data.rationale: A churn-risk score is a predictive classification/regression style output. If the score is based on a trained model over structured signals, L1 is appropriate. I did not choose L0 because the description implies a risk score rather than a simple deterministic rules engine. No LLM is needed because this is not language generation or complex reasoning.

data.label: Evaluate Risk Thresholds
data.description: Route each account based on its churn-risk score.
data.rationale: This is pure threshold-based branching logic over a numeric score. L0 is sufficient because the conditions are explicit and deterministic.

data.label: Notify CSM
data.description: Immediately notify the assigned Customer Success Manager for high-risk accounts.
data.rationale: Sending a notification to a known recipient is deterministic automation. L0 is appropriate because this step is a direct action with no need for ML or language understanding.

data.label: Draft Retention Email
data.description: Generate a personalized retention outreach email for the account.
data.rationale: This step requires language generation to produce a personalized outreach email. L3 is appropriate because a single LLM can draft the email from account context without needing external tools or multi-agent coordination.

data.label: Queue Weekly Review
data.description: Add moderate-risk accounts to the weekly CSM review queue.
data.rationale: Adding an item to a queue is deterministic workflow routing. L0 is sufficient because it is a simple data operation based on an already computed threshold.

data.label: Continue Monitoring
data.description: Keep low-risk accounts under passive monitoring.
data.rationale: This is a straightforward state transition to remain in monitoring mode. L0 applies because no intelligence or generation is required.

data.label: Log Scoring Decision
data.description: Record the churn score and input signals for audit purposes.
data.rationale: Audit logging is deterministic persistence of inputs and outputs. L0 is sufficient because this step simply records structured data for traceability.

message: This workflow is mostly deterministic automation (L0) for data collection, branching, notifications, queueing, and audit logging. One step uses NLP sentiment detection (L2), one step likely uses supervised predictive scoring (L1), and one step drafts personalized email with an LLM (L3). No multi-agent orchestration is required.

workflow.workflowBrief: Monitor existing customer accounts for churn-risk signals: drop in product usage over the last 30 days, support tickets tagged negative-sentiment, and late or failed invoice payments. Score each account's churn risk from 0 to 100. For scores above 75, immediately notify the assigned Customer Success Manager and draft a personalized retention outreach email. For scores between 40 and 75, add the account to a weekly CSM review queue. For scores below 40, continue passive monitoring. Log every scoring decision with the input signals for audit.
